query: What goal-management practices support high achievement?

per_column.name: primary_intervention_type
per_column.rationale: The type of intervention/lever used is a constitutive aspect of how a goal is managed -- a 'what practice' facet of goal-management practice.

per_column.name: timeframe_specificity
per_column.rationale: How specifically the goal is bounded in time is a genuine aspect of goal-management discipline (time-bounding), a facet of the practice itself.

per_column.name: baseline_referenced
per_column.rationale: Whether a baseline is referenced is an aspect of the goal-setting/measurement discipline -- a part of good goal management practice.

per_column.name: measurement_mechanism
per_column.rationale: The mechanism by which progress is measured is a constitutive facet of goal management (the measurement dimension of a practice).

per_column.name: metric_category_alignment
per_column.rationale: Alignment between metric and category is an aspect of goal-definition coherence, a facet of the practice, though it overlaps with the measurement dimension.

per_column.name: scope_of_change
per_column.rationale: The organizational scope targeted is a legitimate aspect of how a goal/practice is framed -- a scoping facet.

per_column.name: multi_lever_approach
per_column.rationale: Whether multiple levers are used is largely a derivative/restatement of primary_intervention_type (breadth of intervention), overlapping with the intervention-type facet rather than adding an orthogonal aspect.

per_column.name: technology_enablement
per_column.rationale: Technology enablement substantially overlaps with intervention_type values like 'automation'/'system_kpi'; it re-expresses part of the intervention facet rather than carving a distinct aspect.

judge.rationale: Most columns are genuine part-of facets of goal-management practice, spanning intervention type, time-bounding, measurement discipline, and scope. However mutual exclusivity is weakened by clustering: baseline_referenced, measurement_mechanism, and metric_category_alignment all address the measurement/definition aspect, while multi_lever_approach and technology_enablement overlap with primary_intervention_type. Exhaustiveness is moderate: the set covers the 'what/when/how-measured/where' dimensions but omits key goal-management facets such as ownership/accountability, prioritization, progress-monitoring cadence, and stakeholder engagement, so it does not fully cover the concept's constitutive aspects.
